prosody.lang: A king turned a mountaintop into his tomb so he could sit beside the gods. At the end of the path a huge mound rises before you. Thousands of fist-sized broken stones were carried up and piled here by hand. Beneath them lies King Antiochus the First of Commagene. His burial chamber has never been found. Antiochus believed he was related to the gods. So he set giant statues on the terrace: Zeus, Apollo, Heracles, the guardian goddess of his kingdom, and himself, all seated side by side. Then the earthquakes came. The heads broke off and rolled down. Now those giant faces rest on the ground at your height, looking you straight in the eye. On a carved stone nearby, the king shakes hands with a god. He traces his family to the Persian kings and to Alexander the Great, as if telling us East and West meet in him. Now sit on a rock and wait for the sun. The light reaches the mound first, then the faces. When you see a stone face turn from pink to gold, you will understand why a king chose this place.
